questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Statistical series : Released by
1. Consumer Price Index : Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
2. Wholesale Price Index : Office of the Economic Adviser, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
3. Index of Industrial Production : Reserve Bank of India
4. National accounts (GDP and GVA) : Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The statistics ministry compiles the national accounts, the Index of Industrial Production and the Consumer Price Index, so pair 3 is wrong. The Wholesale Price Index comes from the commerce ministry, which has also introduced a Producer Price Index. In the 2026 revisions the base year became 2022-23 for GDP, the industrial index and wholesale prices, and 2024 for consumer prices.

questions.q:
With reference to the Producer Price Index introduced in India in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It tracks the prices producers pay for inputs and the prices they receive for output separately.
2. It excludes indirect taxes and transport costs.
3. It covers goods only and leaves out services.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The index is meant to measure prices at the producer's gate, which is why taxes and transport are kept out; the Wholesale Price Index does not make this separation. Statement 3 is wrong: the new index covers services as well as goods, while the wholesale index is confined to goods. The plan is to retire the wholesale index in five years, leaving the consumer and producer indices as the two headline measures.

questions.q: The 'double deflator' method, now used in India's national accounts for agriculture and manufacturing, means that
o: nominal output is deflated first by wholesale and then by consumer prices
real value added is obtained by deflating output and inputs separately with their own price indices
growth is estimated twice, from the production side and the expenditure side
the deflator is revised twice a year using advance and revised estimates
questions.e: Value added is output minus intermediate inputs. Under single deflation the nominal figure is deflated by one price index, which misstates real growth when input and output prices move differently. Double deflation converts output and inputs to constant prices separately and then subtracts. Other changes in the 2022-23 series are the use of GST and labour-force survey data and splitting the output of multi-activity firms across the sectors in which they operate.

questions.q:
With reference to the statistical revisions of 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The new series of the Index of Industrial Production covers only mining and manufacturing and leaves out electricity.
2. The double deflator method is now applied to every sector in the national accounts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither statement is correct. The new industrial index keeps mining, manufacturing and electricity, splits electricity into renewable and non-renewable sources, and adds gas supply, water supply, sewerage and waste management. Double deflation, which deflates output and inputs separately, is so far applied to agriculture and manufacturing, with other sectors to follow.

questions.q:
With reference to the new series of the Consumer Price Index, consider the following statements:
1. Its basket and weights are based on the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023-24.
2. The number of groups in the index has been raised from six to twelve.
3. House rent in rural areas has been brought into the index.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three statements are correct. The earlier basket reflected spending patterns about fifteen years old and still carried items such as cassettes and DVD players. The new one has 358 items against 299, adds rural rent, online media, CNG and piped gas, and measures telephone charges, fares and streaming services better. The index matters because the Monetary Policy Committee targets it, and inflation measures also drive dearness allowance and relief.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The new series of the Index of Industrial Production covers fewer sectors than the series it replaced.
Statement-II: The new series has 2022-23 as its base year and shows electricity generation separately for renewable and non-renewable sources.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct. The coverage has been widened: gas supply, water supply, sewerage and waste management have been added to mining, manufacturing and electricity. The item basket is also larger, and minerals are shown by type. The base year has moved from 2011-12 to 2022-23, in line with the national accounts into which the index feeds.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: An outdated consumer price basket can distort the conduct of monetary policy in India.
Statement-II: The Monetary Policy Committee of the Reserve Bank of India is mandated to target inflation measured by the Wholesale Price Index.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect. The inflation target is defined in terms of the Consumer Price Index, so a basket that no longer reflects what households buy gives the Committee a wrong reading of inflation. Stale deflators also distort real growth figures used in international comparison. The International Monetary Fund had given India's national-accounts statistics a 'C' grade, the second lowest, which was one reason for the overhaul.

questions.q:
With reference to fertiliser subsidies in India, consider the following statements:
1. Urea is sold at a maximum retail price fixed by the government, which bears the gap between that price and the cost of supply.
2. Under the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme, the retail price of di-ammonium phosphate is fixed by the government.
3. Subsidy rates under the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme are fixed for nitrogen alone.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Urea has an administered price, so the gap from production or import cost falls on the budget. For non-urea fertilisers the scheme, in force since April 2010, gives a fixed subsidy per kilogram of nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and sulphur and leaves the retail price to companies, so statements 2 and 3 are wrong.

questions.q:
With reference to the delivery of fertiliser subsidy in India, consider the following statements:
1. Under the direct benefit transfer system, the subsidy amount is credited to the bank account of the farmer.
2. The subsidy is released on the basis of the quantity a manufacturer produces, without reference to sales.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither statement is correct. Under the system in use since 2018, farmers continue to buy at subsidised prices, and the subsidy goes to the manufacturer, not to the farmer's account. It is released only after the retailer's sale is authenticated and captured on a point-of-sale machine, so production alone does not earn it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India's fertiliser subsidy for 2026-27 is projected to be about half the amount provided in the Budget.
Statement-II: India depends heavily on imports of fertilisers and their raw materials, and the West Asia conflict has raised global commodity prices.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct. Because of import dependence and the rise in world prices, the bill is projected at about Rs 3.4 trillion, double the budget estimate of Rs 1.7 trillion and above the earlier peak of Rs 2.5 trillion in 2022-23. A cut in the special additional excise duty on fuels added to the fiscal strain.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Fertiliser : Principal nutrient supplied
1. Urea : Nitrogen
2. Di-ammonium phosphate : Phosphorus, along with some nitrogen
3. Muriate of potash : Potassium
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. Urea is the most widely used nitrogen fertiliser and is central to rice, wheat and sugarcane. Di-ammonium phosphate is the main concentrated source of phosphorus and supports root growth. Muriate of potash is the chief potassium input and improves disease resistance and crop quality. India imports a large part of its needs, most of all potash, which is why its subsidy bill follows world prices.

questions.q: To offset fiscal pressure in 2026-27, the government has been selling minority stakes in listed public sector undertakings through the 'Offer for Sale' route. In this route
o: existing shareholders such as the promoter sell their shares through the stock exchange platform
the company buys back its own shares from the market
shares are allotted to select institutional investors through a private placement
a company issues fresh shares to the public for the first time
questions.e: An Offer for Sale transfers shares already held by the promoter, here the government, to investors through a window on the stock exchanges; the company receives no new capital. The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management has used it regularly and raised about Rs 18,500 crore in the first quarter. The proceeds count towards miscellaneous capital receipts. A fresh issue raises money for the company, and a buyback moves cash in the opposite direction.
questions.s: Shankar IAS p. 102; mechanics of OFS are static

questions.q: In 2026 the Finance Ministry and the Reserve Bank of India were in discussions on the inclusion of Indian government securities in the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Index. The main purpose of seeking such inclusion is to
o: obtain a higher sovereign credit rating automatically
qualify for concessional loans from multilateral lenders
attract foreign portfolio investment into government debt
allow Indian banks to hold foreign government bonds
questions.e: When a country's bonds enter a widely tracked global index, funds that follow the index must buy them, which brings steady foreign portfolio inflows, lowers borrowing costs and supports the currency. The effort is part of the response to the fiscal and external strain of 2026-27, along with stepped-up disinvestment. Index inclusion does not itself change a credit rating or give access to concessional finance.

questions.q:
With reference to the Eighth Central Pay Commission, consider the following statements:
1. It functions under the Department of Personnel and Training.
2. Its recommendations, once accepted by the Centre, are binding on the State governments.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither statement is correct. The commission works under the Department of Expenditure in the Ministry of Finance. Constituted on 3 November 2025 under Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai, it is to report within eighteen months. States are not bound; they usually adopt the recommendations with changes, which is why it must weigh the effect on State finances.

questions.q: 'Non-Functional Upgradation', a contested feature of pay structures discussed in the context of the Eighth Central Pay Commission, refers to
o: the conversion of contractual posts into regular posts
promotion to a higher post without any increase in pay
an allowance for officers posted in non-family stations
the grant of a higher pay level without promotion to a post carrying higher responsibility
questions.e: The device gives officers the pay of a higher grade when their batch-mates in another service reach it, even though they remain in the same post. It was brought in to compensate for slow promotions, but critics say it loosens the link between role, accountability and pay. It is one of the parity questions, along with allowances and the difference between short military and long civilian careers, that the commission is asked to address.

questions.q:
With reference to the terms of reference of the Eighth Central Pay Commission, consider the following statements:
1. It has to take into account the unfunded cost of non-contributory pension schemes.
2. It has to consider the pay and working conditions prevailing in central public sector undertakings and the private sector.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct. The commission must also keep in view economic conditions and fiscal prudence, the need to leave resources for development and welfare, and the likely impact on State finances. A reform idea put forward in 2026 is to replace the once-a-decade commission with a standing body, such as a National Compensation Authority, which would apply common principles on responsibility, experience and hardship.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Larger dividend payments by foreign-owned companies to their parents abroad do not, by themselves, reduce India's net foreign direct investment.
Statement-II: In the balance of payments, dividends are recorded as investment income in the current account, whereas net foreign direct investment is recorded in the financial account.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second explains the first. Dividends widen the current account deficit but leave the direct-investment entry untouched. Net direct investment falls when foreign investors sell their holdings and take the capital out, or when Indian firms invest abroad, since both are financial-account flows. The 2026 analysis therefore attributes the fall in net inflows mainly to disinvestment and capital repatriation, not to profit remittances.

questions.q:
With reference to foreign direct investment in India, consider the following statements:
1. Net inflows, which peaked in 2020-21, fell to below one billion dollars in 2024-25.
2. Conversion of an earlier external commercial borrowing into equity is counted in gross inflows although no new money enters the country.
3. Investment made abroad by Indian companies reduces the net figure.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three statements are correct. Net inflows were 44 billion dollars in 2020-21 and recovered only to 7.6 billion dollars in 2025-26 even though gross inflows were about 94.6 billion dollars. Gross numbers mix fresh capital with intra-group reorganisations, share swaps and debt conversions. The net figure is inflows less repatriation and outward investment, much of which goes to holding companies in Singapore and the United Arab Emirates.

questions.q: In discussions on the quality of foreign investment, 'round-tripping' refers to
o: repeated buying and selling of the same shares to inflate trading volume
repatriation of export earnings within the period fixed by the central bank
reinvestment of a foreign company's profits in the host country
domestic money sent abroad and brought back as foreign investment, usually through an offshore centre
questions.e: Funds leave the country, pass through an entity in a low-tax jurisdiction and return dressed as foreign direct investment, often to gain tax or regulatory advantages. The 2026 analysis places such flows in a third class of investors, diaspora money and special purpose vehicles, about 17.6 per cent of recent inflows, alongside traditional multinationals and financial investors such as private equity. Rising outward investment may partly be the first leg of this circuit.

questions.q:
With reference to India's outward foreign direct investment between 2023-24 and 2025-26, consider the following statements:
1. The greater part of it went into manufacturing units set up abroad.
2. Singapore was the leading destination.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Of about 65 billion dollars invested abroad, some 45 per cent went to financial, insurance and business services, mostly holding companies and special purpose vehicles, not operating plants. Singapore took about 27 per cent and the United Arab Emirates 11 per cent. Outward investment routed through GIFT City also grew. The pattern suggests that such flows cannot be read simply as a sign of corporate maturity.

questions.q:
Which of the following payments by foreign-invested companies in India are recorded in the current account of the balance of payments?
1. Dividends remitted to the parent company
2. Royalty paid for the use of intellectual property
3. Proceeds of the sale of the foreign investor's shareholding taken out of the country
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Dividends are primary income and royalties are payments for services, so both belong to the current account. Sale proceeds repatriated by a foreign investor reverse an earlier capital inflow and are recorded in the financial account, where they reduce net direct investment. The analysis notes that royalty and technical-fee payments can substitute for dividends, and that taken together these outflows now exceed fresh inflows.

questions.q:
With reference to India's revised model Bilateral Investment Treaty of 2026, consider the following statements:
1. An investor must pursue local remedies for at least two years before going to international arbitration.
2. It restores the most-favoured-nation clause that the 2016 model had dropped.
3. Disputes over taxation are kept outside its scope.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The waiting period comes down from the five years associated with the 2016 model, and commercial courts are being promoted for such disputes. The most-favoured-nation clause stays out, so statement 2 is wrong; its absence prevents an investor from importing better terms from India's treaty with another country. The tax carve-out reflects the Vodafone and Cairn arbitrations.

questions.q: 'Treaty shopping', which India's model investment treaty seeks to prevent, refers to
o: a State renegotiating all its investment treaties at the same time
an investor structuring an investment through a third country to gain the benefit of a more favourable treaty
an investor choosing between domestic courts and international arbitration
a State offering tax holidays to compete for foreign investment
questions.e: An investor with no real link to a country routes the investment through it, or relies on a most-favoured-nation clause, to claim protections negotiated for someone else. Leaving out that clause closes one route. India's stricter approach followed adverse arbitral awards; in 2017 it sent termination notices to 68 treaty partners. The 2026 model is described as a middle path between investor protection and the State's right to regulate.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. India sends notices terminating its investment treaties with 68 countries
2. India adopts a model investment treaty requiring exhaustion of local remedies
3. India signs an investment treaty with the United Arab Emirates with a three-year local-remedy period
4. India adopts its first, investor-friendly model investment treaty
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The first model dates from 1993 and led to treaties with over eighty countries and to costly disputes. A stricter model was approved in December 2015 and adopted in January 2016. Termination notices to renegotiate older treaties went out in 2017. The treaty with the United Arab Emirates, which cut the local-remedy period from five years to three, came later and anticipated the further relaxation in the 2026 model.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India's model investment treaty excludes taxation measures from its coverage.
Statement-II: The 2026 model reduces the period for which a foreign investor must pursue remedies in Indian courts before starting international arbitration.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct, but the second does not explain the first. The exclusion of tax matters is a response to arbitration claims brought by Vodafone and Cairn over retrospective taxation. The shorter local-remedy period is a separate change, made because the 2016 model was seen as leaning too far towards sovereignty and deterring investors at a time when partners such as the United Kingdom and the European Union are negotiating treaties with India.

questions.q:
With reference to India's investment treaty practice, consider the following statements:
1. Indian investment treaties do not give a foreign investor a right to make an investment; protection applies only after the investment is made.
2. With Brazil, India has signed an Investment Cooperation and Facilitation Treaty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct. Indian treaties cover the post-establishment phase, so entry remains governed by the foreign investment policy. Standard clauses deal with fair and equitable treatment, national treatment, expropriation and dispute settlement. After the 2016 model India signed treaties with Belarus, the Kyrgyz Republic, the United Arab Emirates and Uzbekistan, and the facilitation-style treaty with Brazil, which relies on dispute prevention.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Platform of the Ministry of MSME : Purpose
1. MSME Sambandh : Monitoring of public procurement from micro and small enterprises
2. MSME Samadhaan : Cases of delayed payment to micro and small enterprises
3. CHAMPIONS : Redress of grievances of enterprises
4. Udyam Assist : Export credit guarantee for medium enterprises
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Sambandh tracks purchases by central public sector enterprises, Samadhaan lets enterprises file delayed-payment cases, and CHAMPIONS is the grievance portal. Pair 4 is wrong: Udyam Assist is the platform for bringing informal micro enterprises into the formal Udyam registration system. Registration opens access to credit, procurement preferences and legal remedies.

questions.q:
With reference to credit support for micro, small and medium enterprises, consider the following statements:
1. The ceiling for collateral-free guarantee cover under the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises has been raised to Rs 10 crore.
2. The Self-Reliant India Fund gives collateral-free working-capital loans to micro enterprises.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The guarantee ceiling was doubled from Rs 5 crore. The Self-Reliant India Fund is an equity vehicle: it invests in growth-oriented enterprises through venture and private equity funds, and received an additional Rs 2,000 crore. A digital credit assessment model that uses data in place of collateral for appraisal is the third element of the credit reforms.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a credit-linked subsidy scheme for setting up new micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector?
o: Micro and Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme
questions.e: The Programme gives a margin-money subsidy on bank loans for new units and now accepts applications in several regional languages. PM Vishwakarma is for traditional artisans and combines skilling, a toolkit incentive and concessional collateral-free loans. The Champions scheme has innovative, sustainable and competitive pillars, including Zero Defect Zero Effect certification and lean manufacturing. The cluster programme funds common facility centres.

questions.q:
With reference to micro, small and medium enterprises in India, consider the following statements:
1. Enterprises are classified on a composite criterion of investment in plant and machinery or equipment and annual turnover.
2. The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 requires buyers to pay micro and small suppliers within a period not exceeding forty-five days.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct. The sector is governed by the 2006 Act, and since 2020 classification rests on both investment and turnover. The Act's delayed-payment provisions, with compound interest on overdue amounts, are enforced through facilitation councils and the Samadhaan portal. The sector accounts for about three-tenths of GDP and nearly half of exports, and delayed payments and costly long-term finance remain its main constraints.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 85-87; classification and the 45-day rule are static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Scheme or body : Purpose
1. PM Vishwakarma : Equity support for technology start-ups
2. ASPIRE : Incubation centres and livelihood training for rural enterprise
3. National SC-ST Hub : Credit guarantee for exporters
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 2 is correct. PM Vishwakarma supports traditional artisans with skilling, toolkits and concessional loans. ASPIRE promotes innovation, rural industry and entrepreneurship. The National SC-ST Hub helps Scheduled Caste and Tribe entrepreneurs with vendor development and public procurement; it is not an export-credit body.

questions.q: 'Drop shipping', a model that has spread through social-media commerce, is best described as an arrangement in which the seller
o: imports goods in bulk and sells them from its own warehouse
delivers goods through a network of local kirana shops
sells only refurbished goods returned by other customers
takes orders without holding stock and passes them to the maker or wholesaler, who ships to the buyer
questions.e: The drop shipper is an intermediary who never buys or stores the product, earns a mark-up and may sit in a chain of several such intermediaries. Low entry cost and AI-run storefronts have made it popular with online creators. The risks are price inflation at each tier, counterfeit or defective goods, delays, and no clear accountability, especially when the deal is moved to a messaging app.

questions.q:
With reference to drop shipping, consider the following statements:
1. It is prohibited in India under the rules on e-commerce framed under the consumer protection law.
2. It lets a buyer purchase a single unit, since no minimum order quantity applies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Drop shipping is lawful in India and elsewhere so long as tax and transparency requirements are met; the concern is with deceptive practice, not the model. The suggestions made are mandatory business and GST registration, liability of virtual intermediaries for product safety and refunds, stricter know-your-customer checks by platforms and clear labelling of AI-generated product advertisements.

questions.q: Consumers buying from unverified online sellers are advised to prefer payment methods that offer 'escrow' or 'chargeback'. An escrow arrangement is one in which
o: the bank reverses a card payment on the customer's complaint
the payment is held by a third party and released to the seller only when the agreed conditions are met
the seller deposits a security amount with the platform before listing goods
the buyer pays in instalments after delivery
questions.e: In escrow a neutral intermediary holds the money until delivery or another condition is fulfilled. A chargeback is different: it is the reversal of a completed card transaction by the issuing bank after a dispute. Both give the buyer a remedy that a direct, irreversible transfer to the seller's account does not, which is why they are recommended for purchases through social-media storefronts.

questions.q:
With reference to 'The State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture 2026', consider the following statements:
1. India is the second-largest producer of aquatic animals in the world.
2. India is the largest producer in aquaculture.
3. At the global level, capture fisheries continue to produce more than aquaculture.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. India has about 9 per cent of world output of aquatic animals, second to China. In aquaculture China leads and India is second with about 12 per cent, so statement 2 is wrong; India does lead in inland capture. Statement 3 is wrong because aquaculture output reached a record and is now ahead of capture fisheries.

questions.q: 'The State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture', whose 2026 edition placed India second in the production of aquatic animals, is published by the
questions.e: The report is a flagship publication of the Food and Agriculture Organization, brought out every two years. The 2026 edition put world fisheries and aquaculture production at a record, with more than nine-tenths of aquatic animal output going to human consumption. The same organisation publishes the reports on food security and nutrition and on the world's forests.
questions.s: Shankar IAS p. 88; periodicity is static

questions.q:
With reference to the findings of 'The State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture 2026', consider the following statements:
1. The share of marine fish stocks fished within biologically sustainable limits declined between 2021 and 2023.
2. Africa has the highest per capita availability of aquatic foods among the regions of the world.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The share of sustainably fished marine stocks slipped from 64.5 to 62.4 per cent, a sign of overfishing, illegal fishing and climate stress. Per capita availability is highest in Asia, at about 26 kg, and lowest in Africa, at about 9 kg, although Africa still draws nearly a fifth of its animal protein from aquatic foods.

questions.q:
Which of the following countries are among the five largest producers of farmed aquatic animals, according to 'The State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture 2026'?
1. Indonesia
2. Vietnam
3. Norway
4. Bangladesh
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The five are China, Indonesia, Vietnam, Bangladesh and India, all in Asia, and together they produce about 82 per cent of farmed aquatic animals. Norway is a major salmon farmer but is not in this group. India's growth is linked to the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana of 2020, the Blue Revolution programme and shrimp exports.

questions.q: The Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund supports the fisheries sector mainly by
o: insuring fishing vessels against cyclone damage
financing fishing harbours, cold storage, processing units and marketing facilities
paying a monthly allowance to fishers during the seasonal fishing ban
questions.e: The Fund provides concessional finance for infrastructure, which addresses post-harvest losses caused by weak cold chains. It works alongside the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana, which aims to raise output and exports and modernise the sector. The remaining concerns are coastal stocks close to their sustainable limits, disease in shrimp farms, salinity intrusion and loss of mangroves from aquaculture.

questions.q:
Match the Labour Codes in List-I with the number of central labour laws each has subsumed in List-II:
List-I
A. Code on Wages
B. Industrial Relations Code
C. Code on Social Security
D. Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code
List-II
1. Three
2. Four
3. Nine
4. Thirteen
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Code on Wages merged four laws, including those on minimum wages and bonus; the Industrial Relations Code three, including the laws on industrial disputes and trade unions; the Code on Social Security nine, including provident fund, state insurance and maternity benefit; and the safety code thirteen, including the Factories and Mines Acts. Together they replace 29 laws and took effect on 21 November 2025.

questions.q:
With reference to the Industrial Relations Code and the Central Rules framed under it, consider the following statements:
1. Establishments with up to 300 workers no longer need prior government permission for retrenchment, against the earlier limit of 100.
2. The Code places a ceiling on the number of times a fixed-term contract may be renewed.
3. The requirement that a sole registered trade union must have at least 30 per cent of the workers as members to be recognised is found in the Rules and not in the Code.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The higher threshold gives employers more room to adjust the workforce. Neither the Code nor the Rules fix a minimum tenure or a limit on renewals of fixed-term employment, so statement 2 is wrong; the fear is that regular posts will be turned into repeatedly renewed contracts. The membership threshold in the Rules means that registration no longer assures recognition for a small union.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The norm for fixing minimum wages retained under the Code on Wages has been criticised as biased against women.
Statement-II: The norm treats a family of four as three consumption units, counting an adult woman as 0.8 of a unit against 1.0 for an adult man.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second explains the first. The Rules laid down no fresh principles, so the old method of counting consumption units continues. Critics say it conflicts with equal pay for equal work. A related complaint is that the hourly wage is derived by dividing the daily wage by eight, which short-changes domestic, informal and gig workers who seldom get eight continuous hours of work.

questions.q:
With reference to the Code on Social Security, 2020 and its Rules, consider the following statements:
1. Gig and platform workers are treated as employees of the aggregator for the purpose of provident fund.
2. The Code provides for a social security fund for gig workers to which aggregators contribute.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The Code recognises gig and platform workers for the first time and creates an aggregator-financed fund for their welfare. It does not make them employees: they remain self-employed persons in the unorganised sector, so the usual employer obligations on provident fund, insurance and safety do not apply. The Rules are also silent on how the mandatory gratuity insurance is to work.

questions.q: Under the Code on Wages, 2019, the 'floor wage' is
o: the minimum wage notified by a State government for unskilled work
the wage paid under the rural employment guarantee programme
a baseline wage fixed by the Central Government below which no State may fix its minimum wage
the lowest wage agreed in a settlement between a union and the employer
questions.e: The floor wage is a national baseline set by the Centre, which may vary by region; minimum wages notified by the appropriate government cannot be lower. Minimum wages themselves continue to be fixed by the Centre and the States for their spheres. The criticism of the Rules is that they do not spell out the distinction clearly and give no binding framework for the consultation with States that the Code requires.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the criticism of the Central Rules under the Labour Codes is not correct?
o: The Rules do not specify the 'core' activities in which contract labour may not be used.
The Rules fix a minimum tenure of one year for fixed-term employment.
The Rules give no working details of the gratuity insurance that the Social Security Code makes mandatory.
Housing and medical facilities long assured to plantation workers do not find a place in the new rules on occupational safety.
questions.e: A minimum tenure of one year for fixed-term employment was suggested but not adopted, so very short contracts remain possible. The other three are gaps that critics have listed: the core and non-core distinction is left undefined, which could allow contract labour in core factory work; sector-specific welfare for plantations has been dropped; and the mechanics of gratuity insurance against employer default are missing.

questions.q:
Which of the following indicators have been dropped from the sixth round of the National Family Health Survey?
1. Prevalence of anaemia
2. Infant mortality rate
3. Sex ratio at birth
4. Spousal violence
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Anaemia, the neonatal, infant and under-five mortality rates, the overall sex ratio and sex ratio at birth, access to sanitation and clean cooking fuel, and screening for cervical, breast and oral cancer have been left out. Spousal violence is still measured and fell from 29.3 to 22.3 per cent. The number of indicators is down from 131 to 101, which breaks the comparability that made the survey valuable.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Anaemia has not been measured in the sixth round of the National Family Health Survey.
Statement-II: Capillary blood taken by finger-prick and tested on portable analysers was considered to overstate anaemia, and its measurement has been shifted to a survey that uses venous blood.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second gives the official reason. Anaemia will be estimated through the Diet and Biomarkers Survey of the National Institute of Nutrition. The earlier round had shown anaemia rising among children, women and pregnant women, which raised questions about the Anaemia Mukt Bharat programme, so the change leaves a gap in the data at a sensitive time.

questions.q:
With reference to the sixth round of the National Family Health Survey, consider the following statements:
1. Digital literacy and the use of digital financial transactions have been surveyed for the first time.
2. Biological testing for HIV, which had been left out of the previous round, has been brought back.
3. The survey covered all States and Union Territories, including Manipur.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The round also asks about receipt of direct benefit transfers and membership of self-help groups, and tests for hepatitis B and C. Statement 3 is wrong: about 6.8 lakh households were covered in all States and Union Territories except Manipur. The results show gains in antenatal care, institutional deliveries, child stunting and women's use of the internet.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Survey or system : Agency responsible
1. National Family Health Survey : International Institute for Population Sciences, as nodal agency
2. Sample Registration System : Office of the Registrar General of India
3. Diet and Biomarkers Survey : National Institute of Nutrition
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. The family health survey has been conducted for the health ministry since 1992 with the Mumbai-based institute as nodal agency. The Sample Registration System, which will now be the source for infant and child mortality, is run by the Registrar General. The nutrition institute's survey will supply anaemia estimates. The worry is that neither substitute gives the district-level and socio-economic detail of the household survey.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 102-104; the Registrar General's role is static

questions.q:
With reference to the National Family Health Survey, consider the following statements:
1. District-level estimates were first produced in the fourth round.
2. The sixth round has more indicators than the fifth.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The fourth round, 2015-16, gave district estimates and used tablets for data collection. The fifth, 2019-21, added subjects such as disability, menstrual hygiene, death registration and non-communicable diseases and had 131 indicators. The sixth reverses this expansion with 101 indicators, dropping several long-running ones while adding questions on digital access and welfare delivery.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the order in which they were launched:
1. Bombay Plan for road development
2. National Highways Development Project
3. Nagpur Plan for road development
4. Bharatmala Pariyojana
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Road planning began with twenty-year plans prepared under the Indian Roads Congress: the Nagpur Plan from 1943, the Bombay Plan from 1961 and the Lucknow Plan from 1981. The National Highways Development Project of 1998 brought the Golden Quadrilateral and the North-South and East-West corridors. From 2017 its remaining works were merged into Bharatmala, which plans corridors around freight movement.

questions.q: Under the Hybrid Annuity Model used for national highway projects,
o: the government pays 40 per cent of the project cost during construction and the balance to the developer as annuities over the operation period
the government bears the full construction cost and the developer only maintains the road
the private developer bears the full construction cost and recovers it from tolls
the government and the developer share toll revenue equally for thirty years
questions.e: The model mixes the engineering-procurement-construction and build-operate-transfer approaches. The developer arranges the remaining 60 per cent and is repaid through fixed annuities, while the authority collects the toll and so carries the traffic risk. It revived highway construction after private investment dried up, but it has placed large long-term payment obligations on the public balance sheet.
questions.s: Shankar IAS p. 108; annuity mechanics are static

questions.q:
With reference to road development in India, consider the following statements:
1. Unfinished works of the National Highways Development Project were merged into the Bharatmala Pariyojana.
2. The PM GatiShakti National Master Plan uses a GIS-based platform with multiple data layers to plan infrastructure.
3. Brownfield upgradation refers to building a highway on a wholly new alignment through undeveloped land.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Bharatmala aims to link 550 district headquarters with four-lane roads and has over 26,000 km of economic corridors. The master plan of October 2021 overlays more than 200 layers such as forests, rail lines and pipelines to detect conflicts before work starts. Statement 3 describes a greenfield project; brownfield work widens or realigns an existing road within its right-of-way.

questions.q: In highway engineering, 'superelevation', a feature of the new access-controlled expressways, refers to
o: raising the road on an embankment above flood level
providing a higher load-bearing capacity for freight vehicles
building an elevated road over an existing one
raising the outer edge of the road above the inner edge on a curve
questions.e: Superelevation is the banking of the carriageway on curves so that part of the centrifugal force on a vehicle is balanced, allowing safe travel at higher speed. Greenfield expressways combine it with straight alignments and few curves for design speeds of up to 120 km per hour. Their cost is large land acquisition under the 2013 law and many environmental clearances.

questions.q:
With reference to the Zojila tunnel, whose breakthrough was achieved in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It connects Baltal near Sonamarg in Kashmir with Meenamarg in the Drass area of Ladakh.
2. It has been bored along its whole length by tunnel boring machines.
3. It is a twin-tube tunnel with separate tubes for traffic in each direction.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The tunnel, about 13 km long at over 11,500 feet, was built by the New Austrian Tunnelling Method, which uses the surrounding rock as part of the support, not by boring machines. It is a single-tube tunnel carrying traffic in both directions, so statement 3 is also wrong. It will keep the road to Ladakh open in winter.

questions.q: The New Austrian Tunnelling Method, used for the Zojila tunnel and other Himalayan tunnels, is based on the principle of
o: boring the full section with a shielded tunnel boring machine
sinking prefabricated tube sections into a trench and covering them
using the surrounding rock mass itself as part of the load-bearing support
questions.e: The method excavates in stages, applies sprayed concrete and rock bolts quickly, and monitors deformation so that the ground around the opening carries part of the load. It suits geology that changes frequently, since support can be adjusted as conditions are observed. Sinking prefabricated sections describes an immersed tube tunnel, and ground freezing is a separate technique for water-bearing soil.
questions.s: Shankar IAS p. 109; other methods are static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Zojila tunnel will give all-weather road access between the Kashmir Valley and Ladakh.
Statement-II: The tunnel's Kashmir-side end is near Baltal, a base camp for the Amarnath Yatra.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct, but the second does not explain the first. All-weather access follows from the tunnel passing under a pass that snow and avalanches close every winter; this is its strategic value for moving troops and supplies towards the Line of Control and the Line of Actual Control. The location near Baltal is a separate benefit for pilgrims, as are tourism and winter sports in Drass.
